note: Hand review of every representation_language the bulk forced-choice pass proposed. The pass proposed a language on 36 of the 632 crops it read; all 36 were opened and judged one at a time, because those 36 are the whole of what reaches lesson_monitoring_selector's productive gate. A rejected row is withheld from the overlay and stays on the books with its reason; it is not deleted and the count is not quietly shrunk.
what_the_rejections_share: Five of the seven are area_model asserted over a closed outline that contains marks but carries no partition: a child's box with a zigzag in it, two circles with a scribble inside, a drawing of a classroom. Two more are a representation asserted over a page whose content is handwriting or a coloured picture. The model reaches for area_model and fraction_bars on any bounded region; set_grouping (15 proposals), number_line (3) and place_value_chart (1) held up on every one.

data/research_assets/research/student_wo.reason: The crop is handwritten Czech reasoning about times. Two thumbnail circles carry a partition; the figure is not an area model.
A hand-drawn box with a zigzag inside. No partition, no equal parts.
A hand-drawn circle with a scribble inside. No partition.
A hand-drawn circle with a scribble inside. No partition.
A high-contrast drawing of a classroom, blackboard and pupils. Nothing in it is an area model.
A child's coloured drawing folded into panels. The panels are not fraction bars.
Handwritten prose about folding a string into six equal parts, with a loose sketch of the string. The writing names equal parts; the drawing is not a fraction bar.

what_this_review_does_not_cover: The 114 spatial-element fills were not opened one at a time. They were sampled through the twenty-figure pilot and through the 36 crops above, and they cannot reach productive_fit on their own: lesson_monitoring_selector scores spatial elements only after a representation language has already matched, and 78 of the 114 sit on rows whose representation stayed none. A wrong spatial element there is a wrong description, never a wrong pick.
